content.content:
**LY-12 — The OccluderSource, the boundary convention, the broadphase and `version`.**
(a) *Seam.* `occluder_source(body_id) -> OccluderSource` exposes `rects_in(aabb)` and `version(section_id)` with EM-20's names verbatim (names unchanged; the out parameter of LY-12 e and the sibling `static_version` / `leaf_version` are additive). EM-20 names no `body_id` while EM-30 compares geometry only within one body, so each instance's `rects_in` answers in THAT body's frame, in ascending key `(section_id, idx)` (D.9) — the **reserved key set** is stable across a weld, a cut and a restore because an attach renumbers nothing: every piece that can ever exist at a socket (PLATE, JAMB, LEAF; LY-15) owns an `idx` from the template's compile, and a state change only switches slots between active and inactive (an inactive slot is omitted from results exactly like a `leaf_w` 0 rect). What changes on a weld is therefore the *active subset* of the sockets' slots, never a key. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
(b) *Boundary convention — stated once.* Integer coordinates in Layout name pixel CELLS. A stored rect `[x0, x1) × [y0, y1)` therefore *occupies* cells `x0..x1−1`, `y0..y1−1`. **One convention per function, no exceptions** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: every box a caller passes IN (`rects_in`, `solid_in`, `clip_to_footprints`, `leaf_would_overlap`'s foot boxes, D.2, D.9, D.22) is **half-open** `[ax0, ax1) × [ay0, ay1)`; every rect handed OUT by `rects_in` **and by `solid_in`** is the **occupied span** `(x0, y0, x1−1, y1−1)`, so the Emitter's D.6 slab arithmetic is unchanged in code and Body's cell sweep reads the same numbers. (The earlier D.9 "closed query box" is retired; a half-open box of width `w` starting at `ax0` touches cells `floor_div(ax0, c)` to `floor_div(ax0 + w − 1, c)`.) Rule text: "the conservative closed test (EM-20 a, a graze blocks) is applied to the occupied span `[x0, x1−1] × [y0, y1−1]`; `ANCHOR_CLEARANCE_PX` is Chebyshev distance from that span" (D.2). A cell outside every occupied span — the first legal row south of a wall, Pipeline D.12 — is therefore not blocked at its origin, which is what EM-6's "outside every footprint by construction" (EM:157) assumes. The foot box's vertical placement is Body's; Layout's guarantee is stated on rectangles and on whatever box the caller passes: a box whose cells lie outside every occupied span is legal.
**CONFLICT C-1 (one-pixel example, not a rule change; routed to the Emitter owner):** EM:467 (D.6 example), EM:1013 (AC-22) and EM:1014 (AC-23) describe "wall x 408..432" as 25 closed points and reject an anchor at 432; under this rule the wall occupies 408..431, so (432, 200) passes with clearance 1 and (431, 200) fails; AC-22's three probes (540 blocked, 407 clear, 408 blocked) are unchanged. `ANCHOR_CLEARANCE_PX` is confirmed at 1 (range 1-2) and re-sourced to this GDD (Cross-References).
(c) *Broadphase.* A per-body uniform grid, cell `BROADPHASE_CELL_PX` 48, derived, never persisted, rebuilt at build, attach, detach and restore (D.9). One structure serves Body's `solid_in`, the Emitter's segment test and Lighting; the Emitter's ADR candidate 4 ("the broadphase … and whether the spatial index lives in Layout or here", EM:32) is answered: **Layout**. `MAX_FOOTPRINT_RECTS_PER_BODY` is sized to the Controller's performance criterion (PCI:1078: 2,000 rects, ≤ 0.05 ms per actor per tick at P99; spike, GDScript cost [UNV]). Callers issue ONE `solid_in` per actor per tick with the swept bounding box and sweep analytically against the result, never one query per 1-px step. Rejected: an Emitter-owned index (drift, double memory) and engine physics queries (EM-20: nondeterministic).
(d) *`version(section_id)`* is a monotone u32, NOT persisted, reset to 1 on `restore` (the Emitter rebuilds in its own `post_restore`; consumers must treat a restore as an unconditional rebuild signal, because a post-restore `version` can numerically equal a pre-restore cached value). It is bumped by `build_section`, `attach_section`, `detach_section`, `discard_section_geometry`, `layout.doors` and Layout's own `post_restore` (LY-26 c, 1 → 2 for a section with an open leaf). MVP has no prop mutator (props are static); the bump list is closed so a Vertical Slice movable prop adds one entry deliberately. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Which sections are bumped (the rule, stated once):** every section whose rect set can change is bumped, *moved or not*. That is (i) every section whose **socket state changes** — both sections of the seam on a weld and on a cut, including the host section that does not move, because on a weld its PLATE becomes JAMB plus LEAF and on a cut its LEAF (possibly open, `area` > 0) becomes a solid PLATE, so a consumer keyed on `version` that missed the unmoved mate would keep passing light through a solid plate (a see-through-but-solid wall, the failure the secondary design test forbids); and (ii) every section whose body-frame offset changes (every moved section). Each such section also gets the dirty key `SEC/<id>`, and both bodies of the seam get `BODY/<id>` (LY-16, LY-17, LY-27). **Three counters, one contract** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: `static_version(s)` is bumped by every cause above except a leaf change; `leaf_version(s)` is bumped only by `layout.doors` (and by `post_restore`'s self-heal for an open leaf); `version(s)` is the EM-20 name and is bumped whenever either is, so a consumer that rebuilds everything keys on `version` unchanged, while a consumer that can patch (the Emitter's static layer, the weld-preview memo) keys the static layer on `static_version` and the dynamic leaves on `leaf_version`. Animating a door therefore bumps `static_version` 0 times; a stepped slide (a Vertical Slice option, OQ-14 c) costs a leaf patch per tick, never a full static rebuild. All three are not persisted and reset to 1 on `restore`. **`changed_region(section_id)`** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*: a pure ordered read `changed_region(section_id) -> ALL | REGION(box) | FRAME`, valid for bumps applied in the current tick (cleared at the end of the tick; the Emitter reads it in W0 of the same tick, because `emitter.place` runs every tick after the P2 apply; NONE when no bump was applied to the section this tick); derived, never persisted (after a restore every section reports ALL once; `version` already resets to 1). Values: build, discard and `post_restore` = ALL (unchanged); a `layout.doors` leaf change = REGION(union box of the old and new leaf rectangles; Emitter ask E-N, unchanged); `attach_section` (LY-16) and `detach_section` (LY-17): for each of the two socket-host sections REGION(union box of that socket's PLATE, JAMB and LEAF slot rectangles, active and inactive, in the section's body frame); for every other moved section (the absorbed body's remaining sections, or the cut-off component's remaining sections) FRAME = a pure translation of the whole body (`rot_q` 0), geometry and slot sets unchanged. A socket-host section that also moves reports REGION; a reader detects its translation by comparing `section_offset(section_id)` with its cached value. The bumps of `version` and `static_version` are unchanged. The read tells the Emitter what kind of change a `static_version` bump was, so it can re-derive its `body_id` and keep its pair rows across a weld or cut without a full cold rebuild (Emitter S8 against S8b); a reader that does not read it treats every bump as ALL.
(e) *Allocation and the result contract.* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The hot-path API is an **out-parameter** API: `rects_in(aabb, out: QueryBuffer)` and `solid_in(body_id, aabb, out: QueryBuffer)` fill a **caller-owned** `QueryBuffer` and return the record count; they return no array. A function that returned one shared reused buffer would alias between consumers (Body's sweep, the Emitter, Lighting and Interaction's throw all call within one tick) and cannot be both allocation-free and safe under copy-on-write, so each consumer owns one buffer and `clear()` resets its length without releasing capacity. **Record layout (structure of arrays, one index per record):** `keys: PackedInt64Array` — `rect_key = section_id × RECT_KEY_STRIDE + idx` reaches `2^32 − 1`, which overflows a 32-bit element for `section_id >= 2^19`, so the key column is 64-bit; `spans: PackedInt32Array` — four ints per record `(x0, y0, x1−1, y1−1)`, the occupied span in the BODY frame (LY-12 b); `flags: PackedByteArray` — one LY-7 flags byte. Records are in ascending `rect_key`; a rect appears once per call (the broadphase de-duplicates a rect spanning several cells). A value-returning wrapper (`rects_in_copy`) may exist for tools and tests only and is not on a hot path. The steady-state call allocates nothing once each buffer has reached its working capacity. (→ ADR: packed-array buffer layout and the engine cost of `resize`, spike SP-ENG-1.)

### D.9 Rect key, canonical order, leaf index and broadphase cells

The rect key formula (registry: `rect_key_order`) is defined as:

static `idx` = rank of the rect in the template sorted by `(y0, x0, y1, x1, flags)`, dense from 0 · leaf `idx` = `N_static + door_declaration_index` · **socket variant `idx` = `N_static + N_doors + 2 × h + v`**, where `h` is the socket's ordinal among the template's **hatched** sockets in declaration order and `v` is 0 for PLATE and 1 for JAMB (a hatchless socket owns none; a hatch's LEAF is its door's leaf slot) · `rect_key(section_id, idx) = section_id × RECT_KEY_STRIDE + idx` · `rects_in` and `solid_in` return ascending `rect_key` · for a **half-open** query box `[ax0, ax1) × [ay0, ay1)`: `cx0 = floor_div(ax0, BROADPHASE_CELL_PX)`, `cx1 = floor_div(ax1 − 1, BROADPHASE_CELL_PX)` (likewise `cy`), `cells = (cx1 − cx0 + 1) × (cy1 − cy0 + 1)` · **empty-box guard:** if `ax1 <= ax0` or `ay1 <= ay0` the box is empty or inverted, it touches **zero cells**, the query returns nothing (the caller's `QueryBuffer` is cleared) and raises the diagnostic `query_box_empty` — without the guard an inverted box such as `ax1 = ax0 − 200` yields `cx1 < cx0` and a formula product that can be a large positive count (two negative factors) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; G5)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: variant slots added; the closed query box is retired in favour of the one half-open input convention of LY-12 b)*

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `N_static` | int | 0 … `MAX_RECTS_PER_SECTION` | derived at load | static rect count of a template; the leaf indices are appended after it in door declaration order |
| `door_declaration_index` | int | 0 … `MAX_DOORS_PER_SECTION` − 1 | template | order of the door in its template |
| `N_doors` | int | 0 … `MAX_DOORS_PER_SECTION` | template | number of door records (interior doors and hatch doors); each reserves one leaf slot *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| `h` | int | 0 … `MAX_SOCKETS_PER_SECTION` − 1 | template | ordinal of a hatched socket; reserves two variant slots (PLATE `v` 0, JAMB `v` 1) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| `RECT_KEY_STRIDE` | int const | `MAX_RECTS_PER_SECTION` 4096 | this GDD | key stride; `idx < 4096`; lint `RECT_STRIDE_OVERFLOW` if `N_static + N_doors + 2 × N_hatched > 4096` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| `section_id` | int | `1 … 2^20 − 1` (`can_build` returns `CAPACITY` when `next_section_id > 2^20 − 1`, LY-27) | the block | so `rect_key < 2^32`; the key column is 64-bit (LY-12 e) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| `BROADPHASE_CELL_PX` | int | 48 (24–96) | this GDD | uniform-grid cell edge; a rect is inserted in every cell its span overlaps |

**Output Range:** `rect_key` in `[0, 2^32)`, unique and stable across attach, detach, restore and animation (an attach renumbers nothing); a leaf with `leaf_w = 0`, an inactive variant slot and a zero-length variant slot keep their `idx` and their keys are skipped. Lint `RECT_INDEX_DENSE` checks the union of **static, leaf and variant** indices is exactly `0 … N−1`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

**Example:** `fixture_cryo_excerpt` static rects, sorted: idx 0 N wall `[24, 408) × [72, 96)`; idx 1 W wall `[24, 48) × [96, 384)`; idx 2 heater `[240, 336) × [96, 144)`; idx 3 E wall `[384, 408) × [96, 384)`; idx 4 S wall west `[24, 240) × [384, 408)`; idx 5 S wall east `[336, 408) × [384, 408)` — `N_static = 6`, so `door_cryo_s` has leaf `idx = 6`; in section 3 its `rect_key = 3 × 4096 + 6 = 12,294`. A half-open query box `[380, 400) × [100, 112)` gives `cx0 = 7`, `cx1 = floor_div(399, 48) = 8`, `cy0 = 2`, `cy1 = floor_div(111, 48) = 2`, so 2 cells; **at a cell edge** `[96, 144) × [0, 48)` touches exactly cell column 2 (`cx1 = floor_div(143, 48) = 2`) and `[96, 145) × [0, 48)` touches columns 2 and 3. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Socket slots (two fixtures):** `fixture_socket_w2` (an E-facing socket, `line_px` 696, `start_px` 240, `W` 2, on a run that is exactly the span, one hatch door) has `N_static` 0, `N_doors` 1, so LEAF `idx` 0, PLATE `idx` 1, JAMB `idx` 2 (zero-width, omitted in every state); `fixture_socket_w3` (the same socket with `W` 3 on the run `[672, 696) × [192, 432)`) has static rects `[672, 696) × [192, 240)` (`idx` 0, before the span) and `[672, 696) × [384, 432)` (`idx` 1, after it), so `N_static` 2, LEAF `idx` 2, PLATE `idx` 3 (`[672, 696) × [240, 384)`), JAMB `idx` 4 (`[672, 696) × [336, 384)`, 48 px). In section 3 the `fixture_socket_w3` PLATE key is `3 × 4096 + 3 = 12,291`. A 16 × 8 foot box moving 3 px per tick sweeps at most a 22 × 14 box (D.22), which touches at most 4 cells.

### D.22 Query cost model (planning arithmetic, not a rule)

The query cost model formula is defined as:

`cost(query) = t_call + cells × ( t_cell + rects_per_cell × t_dedup ) + t_merge(candidates) + candidates × t_test + N_dyn × t_bbox + t_merge_dyn(N_hit)` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the dynamic leaf / variant list is not in the grid, so every query scans it and merges its hits into the key-ordered output; the earlier model omitted both terms)* and `tests_per_actor_tick = cells(swept_box) × rects_per_cell + sweep_tests` · one `solid_in` per actor per tick with the swept box `[px − 8 − v, px + 8 + v) × [py − v, py + 8 + v)` (half-open), `v = V_RUN`, then an analytic axis-separated sweep (never one query per 1-px step); the per-tick aggregate is `Σ over actors cost(solid_in) + Σ over Emitter and Lighting queries cost(rects_in)` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the earlier model counted AABB tests only and omitted the cell lookup, the de-duplication and merge of a rect that spans several cells, the call overhead, and every non-Body consumer.)*

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cells(swept_box)` | int | ≤ 4 at cell 48 | D.9 | grid cells touched |
| `rects_per_cell` | int | about 4 | planning estimate [UNV] | broadphase density |
| `sweep_tests` | int | about 16 | planning estimate [UNV] | analytic sweep against the candidate list |
| `N_dyn` | int | about 6 (MVP body; up to `MAX_DOORS_LOADED` 48 as a stress bound) | planning estimate [UNV] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | length of the body's dynamic leaf / variant list scanned by every query (bounding-box test each) |
| `t_bbox` | µs | about 0.5–1.5 | **[UNV]** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | one bounding-box reject test per dynamic entry (same order as `t_test`) |
| `t_merge_dyn(N_hit)` | µs | about 1 + 0.2 × `N_hit`, `N_hit` about 0–2 | **[UNV]** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | inserting the dynamic hits into the key-ordered output |
| per-test cost `t_test` | µs | about 0.5–1.5 | **[UNV]**, NOT SOURCEABLE (no GDScript cost data in the engine reference) | one AABB test *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| call overhead `t_call` | µs | about 1–3 | **[UNV]** | one GDScript call, buffer `clear()` and the 64-bit key column writes *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| cell lookup `t_cell` | µs | about 0.5–1 | **[UNV]** | one grid-cell index computation and read *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| de-dup `t_dedup` | µs | about 0.3–0.8 | **[UNV]** | one generation-stamp check per candidate (a rect spanning k cells is met k times) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| merge `t_merge(c)` | µs | about 1 + 0.2 × c | **[UNV]** | ordering the candidates by `rect_key` (insertion into the sorted output) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| Emitter-sized query | box | 288 × 288 px (lamp radius `R_DRAW_MAX_PX` 144) → up to 7 × 7 = 49 cells at cell 48, about 100–200 candidate rects | planning estimate [UNV] | a `rects_in` call from the Emitter's static-layer rebuild or a segment test; amortised by the `static_version` cache (LY-12 d) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| actors per tick | int | 4 seats + the horror entities in range (about 6–8 in the MVP) | planning estimate | the aggregate-actor case *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |

*(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Output Range:** about 32 tests plus the cell, de-dup, merge and call terms, about 0.028–0.072 ms per actor per tick from the static table (low: 1 + 6.8 + 4.2 + 16 = 28 µs; high: 3 + 16.8 + 4.2 + 48 = 72 µs, at 4 cells and 16 candidates), plus the dynamic terms at `N_dyn` 6 and `N_hit` 1 (3–9 µs scan plus 1.2 µs merge), so **about 0.033–0.082 ms, rounded to 0.03–0.08 ms** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the earlier '0.04 to 0.08' did not follow from the table)* — above the Controller's budget of 0.05 ms P99 over 2,000 rects (PCI:1078) at the pessimistic end, which is why the pass lines are spike measurements (group K), not rules; the aggregate for 8 actors is then 0.26–0.66 ms of the 16.6 ms frame (**AC-164's aggregate line of at most 0.6 ms is the budget; AC-136's 0.05 ms P99 per actor is the target**, and the pessimistic end of the model exceeds the line, which is why group K is a spike) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, and an Emitter-sized query is about 0.1–0.3 ms, paid only on a `static_version` change. The model is planning only. **Fallback ladder (cheapest rung first, each a data-layout step):** (1) tune `BROADPHASE_CELL_PX` (24/48/96); (2) replace the sort in `t_merge` with per-cell pre-sorted arrays and a generation-stamp de-dup; (3) cache results keyed by `(cell set, static_version)` for static consumers (the Emitter's static layer already is); (4) merge collinear abutting wall rects at load (fewer rects, same occupied cells); (5) only then a GDExtension or C# rung, which needs technical-director sign-off and is out of the project's GDScript-only stack until granted. The weld's `GEOM_OVERLAP` test is the same arithmetic over the grid (`n_B × c_cell` probes, about 800 for a 200-rect section against brute force's 40,000), memoised for a preview on `(socket_a, socket_b, static_version_a, static_version_b)` (LY-14).

**Example:** a body of 3 sections, 200 rects, an actor mid-room: the swept box `[px − 11, px + 11) × [py − 3, py + 11)` touches 1–4 cells, about 16 candidate rects, about 32 tests in total.

# ADR-0013: Ship Layout Block, Geometry and ID Allocation

## Status
Proposed

## Date
2026-10-29

## Last Verified
2026-10-29 (against `design/gdd/ship-section-and-layout-data-model.md` LY-1 to LY-35 and D.5, D.6, D.9, D.10, D.12, D.21; ADR-0001 to ADR-0010, all Proposed; the engine facts marked "probed 2026-10-29" were run on the 4.7.2 mono console binary)

## Decision Makers
Claude (author), running under modes.automation: autonomous (project.yaml); decisions logged for the user's review; the user has not yet reviewed this ADR.

## Summary
Ship Section & Layout is the one owner of rooms, rectangles, sockets, welds, bodies and three id spaces, and every Core and Feature system reads or calls it, but no document fixes how its block is shaped, how its rectangles are keyed, how a weld moves a body or which side of the Layout/Graph boundary allocates which id. This ADR decides: `layout.state` stores **instances by reference** to immutable catalog templates as **dense per-column packed arrays** (rows addressed by `id - 1`, tombstones kept, a third persisted `structure_hash` added to the GDD's two); geometry is **integer half-open rectangles** with a flags byte in a reserved, never-renumbered `idx` space; sockets are **sparse terminal-state rows** changed only inside two mutators; weld offsets are computed on the **lower-`body_id` survivor** with a canonicalised `welds[]`; and ids are **split** so that Layout allocates `section_id`, `body_id` and `room_id` from persisted counters while the Graph allocates node, edge, compartment and seam ids and Layout only stores the per-instance bases.

## Engine Compatibility

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Engine** | Godot 4.7.2 (pinned 4.7; installed 4.7.2.stable.mono, `docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md`) |
| **Domain** | Core (simulation data model; scene-tree free, integer-only; the PROJECTOR that draws it is ADR-0034's) |
| **Knowledge Risk** | MEDIUM. The module uses no rendering, physics or scene API. The two HIGH items it touches are the 4.7 packed-array element-write change (every dirty mark here is explicit inside a mutator) and the 4.7 typed-return override rule (it applies to the `@abstract` port of § 8; the rule is sourced from `breaking-changes.md` § 4.6 to 4.7) |
| **References Consulted** | `docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md`; `breaking-changes.md` (4.6 to 4.7 GDScript rows, 4.3 `TileMapLayer` row); `deprecated-apis.md`; `current-best-practices.md` § GDScript (4.7). **`docs/engine-reference/godot/modules/` has no core, scripting or tilemap file** (it holds animation, audio, input, navigation, networking, physics, rendering and ui), so every claim about `Array[String]` encoding, packed-array methods and GDScript cost below is either probed or marked UNVERIFIED. Project ADRs: 0001 to 0010 (§ Related) |
| **Post-Cutoff APIs Used** | Packed-array element writes that skip the property setter (4.7); `@abstract` ports (4.5, chosen by ADR-0010) for `LayoutGraphPort`; typed `Array[String]` as a persisted column. No `TileMapLayer`, `Node` or `Resource` API is used by this ADR |
| **Verification Required** | **V1 (probed 2026-10-29, done):** `PackedInt32Array.bsearch(v)` returns the insertion index and, for ties, the first index with `before = true` and one past the last with `before = false`; `PackedInt32Array.insert` and `remove_at` keep order; a value `0xDEADBEEF` stored in a `PackedInt32Array` reads back as `-559038737` and masks to `3735928559`; `var_to_bytes` then `bytes_to_var` returns a typed `Array[String]` still typed and a `PackedInt64Array` exact to 2^40; `PackedStringArray` also round-trips (but ADR-0006 § 1.2 does not allow it in a save, so it is not used); `duplicate()` of a packed array is independent of later element writes. **V2 (UNVERIFIED, spike S1 / SP-ENG-1):** the GDScript cost of the `layout.doors` loop at `MAX_DOORS_LOADED` doors on a release export on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK against its 0.2 ms line (TR-section-042). **V3 (UNVERIFIED, S1 with ADR-0014):** the P2 cost of `attach_section` and `detach_section` including the per-body broadphase rebuild at `MAX_FOOTPRINT_RECTS_PER_BODY`. **V4 (UNVERIFIED, after ADR-0005 is Accepted):** golden vectors for `geometry_hash`, `visual_hash` and `structure_hash` of the four MVP templates, equal on the editor and on the `template_release` export (ADR-0007 CONTENT-EXP-1). **V5 (UNVERIFIED):** `Array[String]` column cost in `snapshot()` and in the type walk for the largest long-campaign shape of § 12 (tens of rows; expected negligible, measured in SAVE-WRK-1 f) |

None is Accepted yet, so this ADR cannot be Accepted before them |

| **Blocks** | The Layout epic (template compile and hashes, `layout.state`, LM1 to LM4, `layout.doors`, read views); every Feature story that calls `build_section`, `attach_section`, `detach_section` or reads `rects_in`/`room_at`/`door_passage` |
| **Ordering Note** | Wave A. ADR-0011 (Graph data model, same wave) must supply the Graph side of § 3 and § 8: the `instantiate_section` return and its contiguity guarantees, the allocation-free `opening` read and the `LayoutGraphPort` implementation (§ Related lists every assumption). ADR-0014, ADR-0015, ADR-0016 and ADR-0034 are written afterwards and build on the records fixed here. Where this ADR and the Layout GDD differ (§ Related, "GDD sync"), the ADR is the proposal and the GDD is updated to it, not the reverse |

### 5. Rectangles, units and frames: the record, the flags and the reserved `idx` space

ADR-0014 owns the broadphase, `QueryBuffer`, `OccluderSource` and the query signatures. This ADR owns **what a rectangle is, how it is keyed and which ones can exist**.

- **The record (TR-section-010).** A rect is `(x0, y0, x1, y1)` in section-local base px, **half-open** `[x0, x1) x [y0, y1)` over pixel cells, with one flags byte: `SOLID`, `OCCLUDES_LIGHT`, `DOOR_LEAF`, `PROP`, `MACHINE`, `HULL` (registry `layout_rect_flags`). The legal flag combinations are LY-7's table and a boot error otherwise (`RECT_FLAGS_ILLEGAL`). A rect with `x1 <= x0` or `y1 <= y0` is omitted from every result but keeps its `idx`.
- **Units and frames.** The unit is the base pixel; `TILE_PX` is the floor tile and `WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` the wall depth. There is no world frame in Layout. Reads answer **section-local** except those that answer for one body (`rects_in`, `solid_in`, `clip_to_footprints`, `leaf_would_overlap`, `section_at`, `weld_offset`, `detach_preview`), which answer in the **body frame** = section-local + `offset_px(section_id)` (LY-3 c).
- **Transforms are integer translation only.** No rotation, no mirror, no zoom value appears anywhere in Layout (LY-3 d, e). Every px-to-tile or px-to-cell conversion is **floor** division through `IntMath.floor_div` (body-frame coordinates may be negative after a detach re-base); the bare `/` and `%` operators appear nowhere in `src/sim/layout/` (ADR-0010 `SIM-05`).
- **The `idx` space is compiled once per template and never changes** (D.9): static rects sorted by `(y0, x0, y1, x1, flags)` are `0 .. N_static - 1`; one reserved leaf slot per door follows in door declaration order; two reserved variant slots (PLATE, JAMB) per **hatched** socket follow, `idx = N_static + N_doors + 2h + v`. The key `(section_id, idx)` is therefore stable across attach, detach, restore and animation: a state change only switches slots between active and inactive; an inactive or zero-length slot is omitted from results and keeps its `idx` (TR-section-020's "renumbers nothing" half).
- **Rect keys.** `rect_key = section_id * RECT_KEY_STRIDE + idx` with the stride `MAX_RECTS_PER_SECTION` (GDD Tuning Knobs, a power of two) and `idx < stride`; the key reaches `2^32 - 1`, so every key column is `PackedInt64Array` (ADR-0014 owns the buffer). Boot refuses a template whose `N_static + N_doors + 2 N_hatched` exceeds the stride (`RECT_STRIDE_OVERFLOW`).
- **The compiled table is catalog data.** `SectionTemplate` exposes rect `idx`-indexed accessors (`rect_count()`, `rect_x0(i)`, `rect_y0(i)`, `rect_x1(i)`, `rect_y1(i)`, `rect_flags(i)`, `rect_owner_kind(i)`, `rect_owner_ref(i)`), never a packed array (ADR-0007 § 1.5). The bulk read that builds a body's grid at build, attach, detach and restore is ADR-0014's; those events are cold, so accessor calls are acceptable there (V3 measures them).
- **Static footprint set versus query set.** `rects_in` returns `OCCLUDES_LIGHT` rects and `solid_in` returns `SOLID` rects in their *current leaf state*; the mating overlap test of § 6 uses the **static** set with all flags, so a door animating can never flip a verdict. Both sets are views of one rect set (Pillar 1: collision, light and drawing cannot disagree); neither is an engine collision shape, and the avatar has no physics body.

### 8. The door leaf, the `layout.doors` hook and the Graph port

**One rectangle per leaf.** A door or hatch has one leaf rect. With `width_px` (the 96-px door cell), the Graph opening's `area` clamped to `[0, area_max]` and `area_max > 0`: `gap = floor_div(width_px * area, area_max)`, `leaf_w = width_px - gap`, and the rect is anchored to the hinge side with depth `WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` (D.5; hinge LOW for every socket hatch so both leaves of a mated hatch retract the same way). `leaf_w = 0` returns no rect and keeps its `idx`. A mated hatch is two leaves (one per section) driven by one `area`.

**The port.** Layout reads and calls the Graph only through `LayoutGraphPort` (`src/sim/layout/ports/layout_graph_port.gd`, `@abstract`, ADR-0010 § 3), implemented by the Graph's facade and injected into `setup()`:

```gdscript
@abstract class_name LayoutGraphPort extends RefCounted
@abstract func check_instantiate(views: SimViews, template_id: String) -> StringName   # Graph CAPACITY pre-check for can_build
@abstract func instantiate_section(scope: WriteScope, section_id: int, template_id: String, kind: int, out: SectionBases) -> int
@abstract func opening_into(edge_id: int, out: OpeningRead) -> bool   # false = unknown edge; fills area, area_max, door_state
@abstract func seam_openings_into(seam_id: int, out: SeamOpenings) -> bool   # opening_ids[] in socket_plan.openings order
@abstract func section_counts_into(section_id: int, out: SectionCounts) -> bool   # nodes, edges, compartments, next_section_id (verification only)
```

The 4.7 typed-return rule applies to any override of a typed-return abstract method, so each implementation returns explicitly on every path (a stub that omits a return is a parse error or a defect found by V-lint). The reads are allocation-free (caller-owned `out`), valid in P3 and in P2 after the Graph's own writes.

**The hook (TR-section-012).** `layout.doors`: `hook_id &"layout.doors"`, owner Layout, `divisor 1`, `offset 0`, `after []`, running in P3. Body's `body.integrate` is registered `after: [controller.step, layout.doors]` (BDY-8), which orders the Emitter after it transitively, so every P3 reader sees same-tick leaves. The hook loops over the `LayoutDerived` leaf cache, a dense list of at most `MAX_DOORS_LOADED` slots in ascending `(section_id, door_index)` (deterministic bump order):

1. `graph.opening_into(edge, op)`. If it returns false (unknown opening) the leaf stays at its last projected value (closed at the template default), `area` is never invented, `leaf_version` is not bumped, and the diagnostic `opening_unknown` is raised **once per edge** (a bit in the slot's flags, cleared when the read succeeds again) (TR-section-035). A `area_max <= 0` read is treated the same way and counted `opening_invalid`.
2. `area` is clamped to `[0, area_max]`; a value above `area_max` raises the diagnostic `area_clamped` and uses `area_max` (TR-section-035).
3. `leaf_w` is computed (integer, `IntMath.floor_div`), compared with the slot's last-projected value, and if different the leaf rect is recomputed and the slot's section is flagged.
4. After the loop, for each flagged section in ascending id: `leaf_version += 1`, `version += 1`, never `static_version`; `changed_region` is stamped REGION(union of the old and new leaf rectangles). **At most one bump per section per tick** (TR-section-042).
5. If any section was flagged, the hook opens `layout.state` once (`scope.open_for`) and marks one **`LEAF/<section_id>`** key per flagged section.

**Why the hook marks a key, and why a new kind.** `layout.doors` changes only derived caches, yet the PROJECTOR must redraw a leaf whose rect changed and the door leaf sprite extent must equal the leaf rect with no tween (TR-section-013). ADR-0009 presenters draw from dirty batches; polling every section's counter every frame would add a read per frame for an event that happens a few times per play. Marking is legal (ADR-0004 § 7: a key marked for an unchanged value is not a violation; the HOOK scope may open any block). Its cost is that a granted `open_for` advances `touch_serial`, invalidating the block hash cache (ADR-0005 § 5.2) on those ticks; under the binary door model that is a few ticks per play, and the re-encode is bounded by the block size (tens of KB). LY-32's closed list is SEC, BODY, SEAM; a leaf change under `SEC/<id>` would also wake Failure & Trail's anchor rebuild and Lighting's static rebuild on every door toggle, so the key family **`LEAF` (kind 4)** is added to Layout's own key space (ADR-0004 § 3 leaves unnumbered families to the owner). Subscribers that care (the PROJECTOR, Lighting's dynamic leaf patch) test `batch.has(key)`; the rest ignore it.

**The correctness condition.** Every `area` write of a template door or mated hatch lands in **P2** by command (a SYSTEM-origin `set_opening` re-submitted each tick by Interaction's `attempts[]` for a `CLOSING_BLOCKED` retry); no Graph phase writes `area` or `door_state` of such an opening (the Graph's virtual breach and seam-weep openings have no leaf and are neither read nor projected). Layout stores, mirrors and writes neither value (TR-section-013); `layout_hash` does not cover door state. This is a cross-ADR assumption on ADR-0011/0012/0020 and a test (AC "closed leaf blocks and an open one does not in the same tick its state changes").

**Seeding.** LM1 reads the just-created openings through the port and derives each leaf immediately (the Graph holds authored initial areas), so there is no tick in which a built door is wrong. **LM2 does not read the Graph's `area`:** it initialises each newly active LEAF **closed** (`leaf_w = width_px`) and seeds the last-projected cache with that value in the same apply, because `weld_join` starts the new opening at `area` 0; reads between the P2 apply and the first P3 hook therefore see a solid span, raise no `stale_leaf`, and the hook bumps `leaf_version` only if its `area` read differs (TR-section-034). `post_restore` derives all leaves in one `derive_doors` pass (§ 10).

**Pure leaf queries.** `leaf_would_overlap(opening_edge_id, area, boxes: PackedInt32Array) -> bool` and `leaf_obstruction_into(opening_edge_id, area, boxes, out: LeafObstruction) -> bool` evaluate **every** leaf projected from that opening (`opening_leaves`: both sections of a mated hatch) at the new `area`, in the body frame, against every caller-supplied foot box (`boxes` is a flat half-open `x0, y0, x1, y1` array the caller owns); Layout reads nothing from `body.state` (TR-section-014). `door_passage_into(section_id, via_id, out: DoorPassage) -> bool` returns `{orientation, sill_rect, gap_rect, open_extent_px}` from the leaf value `layout.doors` last projected (so collision, light and passage cannot disagree and `opening` is not re-read); an unknown or discarded section or `via_id` returns false with no error; before `post_restore` it reports `open_extent_px` 0 and raises `stale_leaf`. The single passability rule is a pure helper `DoorPassage.passable(open_extent_px, orientation, foot_extent_ew, foot_extent_ns)`: passable iff `open_extent_px` is at least the foot extent across the doorway (the Body foot box, BDY-14: 16 across an east-west run, 8 across a north-south run, supplied by Body as constants, not owned here) (TR-horror-032).

**Cost.** The hook is an integer multiply and divide per door plus one port call and compare. Target <= 0.2 ms at `MAX_DOORS_LOADED` animating doors (5 percent of `STEP_BUDGET_MS`) on a release export, a pending-spike figure (V2). The fallback ladder is ADR-0010 § 9: cache accessors in locals, then early-out on an unchanged Graph `touch` counter if ADR-0011 publishes one, before any native rung.

### 1. The block: one `layout.state`, instances by reference, derived state kept apart

Layout registers exactly one block, `layout.state`, with the descriptor values of LY-1 and the fields ADR-0003 requires:

| `BlockDescriptor` field | Value |
|---|---|
| `block_id` / `owner_name` | `&"layout.state"` / `&"layout"` |
| `schema_version` / `supported_versions` | `LAYOUT_BLOCK_SCHEMA_VERSION` (GDD Tuning Knobs, 1) / `[1]` |
| `block_class` / `persist` / `persist_scope` / `scope` | `SIM` / true / `WORLD` / `SHARED` |
| `gameplay` / `interpolated` | true / false |
| `repl_hint` | `SHARED_SUMMARY`: the summary is the instance table plus the three hashes; geometry never travels (templates are identical on every peer by `catalogue_version`) |
| `restore_after` | `[]`: Layout is the root of the restore order and reads no other block in `restore()`; ADR-0016 owns the DAG |
| `snapshot`, `restore`, `default_state`, `post_restore`, `read_view`, `empty_view` | six registered `Callable`s, each ending `return ctx.complete()`; `commit_baseline`/`snap_baseline` absent (not interpolated); `init_world`/`binding_source` absent (Web Map's `init_world` calls LM1; Layout binds nothing) |

**Instances by reference (ADR-LAY-01).** A template is authored, immutable and lives in the frozen `SectionTemplates` catalog; an instance is a row in `layout.state` that names a template by its `template_id` string and carries only what can differ between two instances of one template: its ids, body, offset, id bases, drift hashes and socket/weld history. Full geometry in the block would multiply rectangles by sections, duplicate authored data, defeat the Vertical Slice "seed plus deltas" model and let an exporter bug corrupt the world permanently; a second `layout.templates` block would add a second restore root for nothing. Both are rejected (§ Alternatives 1 and 2).

**Two objects, one owner.** The module owns two plain `RefCounted` objects:

- **`LayoutState`** holds the persisted tables of § 2 as typed fields. It is the object the block descriptor's callables read and write; `restore` copies into it and never replaces it (ADR-0003 § 2), because the read-view facade `LayoutViews` wraps it for the life of the process.
- **`LayoutDerived`** holds everything that is rebuilt from `LayoutState`, the templates and the Graph and is **never snapshotted or hashed**: the `section_id`-indexed lookup columns, the socket-ref index, the live-count caps, the leaf cache and `opening_leaves` map (§ 8), the three version counters and `changed_region` stamps (§ 7), `mutation_count`, and the handle to ADR-0014's broadphase. The split is what makes "derived caches are never persisted" (TR-section-004) checkable: a test snapshots `LayoutState` only, and the allow-list test of AC-130 walks only that payload.

**What the block never holds.** Floats; geometry; the section `kind` (the Graph's section record owns it, LS-17); a `visited` bit (the block is WORLD-scoped and rolls back on `request_restore`); a loose-item table (Interaction's `interaction.state` holds it and lists `layout.state` in its own `restore_after`); a door `area` or `door_state`; atmosphere; pose, velocity or any `body.state` field; a stored `layout_hash` or `mutation_count` (Save/Load's `block_state_hash` owns the stored copy, LY D.10, OQ-36). This is TR-section-028 and the first half of TR-section-013.

**Source layout (ADR-0010).** `src/sim/layout/`: `layout_module.gd` (owner, registration, callables), `layout_state.gd`, `layout_derived.gd`, `layout_ids.gd`, `socket_ref.gd`, `layout_faults.gd`, `layout_mutators.gd` (LM1 to LM4 and checks), `weld_math.gd` and `detach_planner.gd` (pure), `door_leaves.gd` (the hook), `layout_restore.gd` (validation), `views/` (`LayoutViews` and the record classes of § 11), `ports/layout_graph_port.gd` (`@abstract`, § 8). The PROJECTOR is `src/presentation/projector/` and is never imported from here. The pure compile of authored runs into the rect table (`TemplateCompiler`) lives under `src/data/sections/` beside the loader that calls it, owned by Layout by review, not by import (ADR-0007 § 1.9).

### 10. Restore, drift and `post_restore`

**`restore(data, stored_version, ctx)` is two-phase** (ADR-0003 § 2, ADR-0006 § 2.2): decode and validate into a `LayoutScratch` (cold path, allocation allowed); on any failure call `ctx.fault(code, detail)` and write nothing; on success **copy the contents into the existing `LayoutState` object** (each column assigned from the scratch's own arrays, none aliasing `data`), then rebuild the static `LayoutDerived` (lookups, socket index, caps, version counters reset to 1, `mutation_count` 0, memo cleared, broadphase handles rebuilt by ADR-0014's call). A restore swaps whole tables only on success (TR-section-007).

**Validation, in order** (first failure wins, with a named detail): (1) `stored_version` in `supported_versions` and the key set equals the § 2 table, every column has the declared type and equal row counts per table (`LAYOUT_RESTORE_SCHEMA`); (2) every `template_id` resolves in the catalog (`LAYOUT_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_TEMPLATE`); (3) `rot_q` all 0 (`LAYOUT_ROT_UNSUPPORTED`); (4) the drift policy below (`LAYOUT_RESTORE_TEMPLATE_CHANGED`); (5) dense ids: `section_id[i] == i + 1`, `body_id[i] == i + 1`, `room_id_base[i + 1] == room_id_base[i] + rooms(template[i])`, counters equal the dense count + 1 and below the ceilings (`LAYOUT_RESTORE_COUNTER`); (6) references: every non-discarded instance sits on a `LIVE` body, every `LIVE` body has an in-range `origin_section_id` that belongs to it, socket rows are strictly ascending with `socket_index < template.socket_count` and a resolving `seam_id`, weld rows ascend and agree with their socket states (`ACTIVE` with two `WELDED`, `CUT_SEALED` with two `CAPPED`, `CUT_RAGGED` with two `CUT_OPEN`), `ACTIVE` welds form a forest whose components are exactly the `LIVE` bodies' section sets, and every `ACTIVE` weld's offsets satisfy `offset_b = offset_a + pos_a - pos_b` on the 24 grid (`LAYOUT_RESTORE_DANGLING`). An unsupported `stored_version` is a reported failure, never a silent default.

**Drift policy (TR-section-007).** The current template's three hashes are compared with the stored ones after `& 0xFFFFFFFF`. A **`structure_hash`** difference is `LAYOUT_RESTORE_TEMPLATE_CHANGED` for every instance (§ 4). A **`geometry_hash`** difference is `LAYOUT_RESTORE_TEMPLATE_CHANGED` when the instance carries history, meaning any non-`FREE` socket, any `welds[]` row naming it, or a body shared with another section, because a moved socket or wall edge under a welded or cut instance restores with broken abutment; on a never-welded `FREE` instance alone it is accepted with the diagnostic `geometry_changed_fresh`, the rects are re-derived from the new template and the stored hash is rewritten. A **`visual_hash`** difference alone is accepted with `visual_changed` and rewritten. A hash collision cannot hide a structural change that also changes a tile set or key sequence in a way the validation of step (6) detects; a 2^-32 collision on `structure_hash` is accepted and recorded (§ Risks R6). Pre-release saves are disposable; after the first outside build the migration obligation of LY-6 e applies, and a rewritten hash means the next snapshot differs from the stored one, so the K-4 `state_hash` compare reports a mismatch as a diagnostic, as designed.

**Query validity after restore.** Class 1 (static, valid when `restore()` returns): `room_at`, `V`, `exposed_tiles`, `room_surface`, `socket_plan`, `anchor_geometry`, static rect membership, `section_offset`, `body_of`, `section_at`. Class 2 (leaf-dependent, valid after `post_restore()`): `rects_in`/`solid_in` door leaves, `clip_to_footprints`, `leaf_would_overlap`, `door_passage_into`. Between the two they report the template default (every leaf closed) and raise `stale_leaf` if read; `LayoutDerived.leaves_valid` is the flag. The kernel guarantees every `restore()` completes before any `post_restore()` begins.

**`post_restore(ctx)`** (a) runs one `derive_doors` pass over the leaf cache using `opening_into` (an `area` above `area_max` is clamped with a diagnostic, and the same fault found *here* is `LAYOUT_RESTORE_DANGLING`; an unknown opening leaves the leaf closed); (b) rebuilds `opening_leaves` from the restored `welds[]` and `seam_openings_into`; (c) bumps `version` and `leaf_version` (never `static_version`) for each section whose derived leaf set differs from the all-closed default, so a restored open door is a 1 to 2 transition and every rebuilding consumer rebuilds on tick 1 with no ordering between `post_restore` calls; (d) runs cross-block **verification** through `section_counts_into`: every `graph_ref_base` resolves (node, edge and compartment counts match the template), every `welds[]` `seam_id` resolves to a Graph seam record, and `graph.next_section_id == layout.next_section_id`. Failures use the restore codes. Verification order and the "installed `def_id` at a hardpoint resolves" diagnostic belong to ADR-0016's verifier list; this ADR supplies the checks Layout's side can run. After a restore every section reports `changed_region` ALL once, and the kernel delivers one `ALL` batch (ADR-0003 § 4).

**Policy line (TR-derelict-008 Layout half).** A save restores from its **saved values**: templates are never mutated at runtime, a restore never re-templates an instance, and no Authoring content lint runs at restore.

### 11. Read views: records, tiers, order and frames

Reads are pure, side-effect free, deterministic and identical before a snapshot and after restoring it (idempotent), and have **no "perceived" variant** (Pillar 1, TR-section-039). They are exposed through the long-lived `LayoutViews` facade (ADR-0003 § 7); no live container is ever returned. Two tiers:

- **Tier H (hot; allocation-free; tagged `## @hot` for ADR-0010 `HOT-01`; scalar results or caller-owned `out`):** `room_at(section_id, x, y) -> int` (`0` = NONE; a sill px answers its `sill_room`, so no walkable point answers NONE), `floor_tile_at(...) -> int` (`-1` = NONE), `section_at(body_id, x, y) -> int` (`0` = NONE; FLOOR division), `section_offset_x/_y(section_id)`, `body_of(section_id)`, `version`, `static_version`, `leaf_version`, `changed_region_kind/_box_into`, `door_passage_into`, `leaf_would_overlap`, `leaf_obstruction_into`, `V(room_id)`, `exposed_tiles(room_id)`, and ADR-0014's `rects_in`/`solid_in` (sentinels for an unknown or discarded section are `0`/false, never an error).
- **Tier C (cold; may allocate; returns a freshly built immutable record or a typed `Array[Record]`):** `room_surface`, `room_boundary`, `anchor_geometry`, `subject_anchors`, `socket_plan`, `weld_offset`, `detach_preview`, `room_adjacency`, `hull_segments_near`, `loose_slots`, `hardpoints_of`, `segment_at`, `plate_positions`, `sections_of`, `route_length_px`, `south_band`, `wall_face_rows`, `template_hash`.

**Fixed field names, orders and bounds.** Records live in `src/sim/layout/views/` as get-only `RefCounted` classes: `AnchorGeometry {kind, host_face_id, base_px_polyline (PackedInt32Array pairs), sort_origin_y, section_id}`, `RoomSurface {floor_tiles (PackedInt32Array pairs, tile id ascending), wall_faces}` (the Failure & Trail contract, section-local), `DoorPassage` (D.5 table), `RoomAdjacencyRow {room_a, room_b_or_exterior, via (DOOR|HATCH), via_id, sill_room}`, `SubjectAnchor {local_key, kind_hint, anchor_px, room_id, console_role}`. Ordering contracts: `room_adjacency` by `(room_a, via_id)`; `subject_anchors` and the slot reads by key ascending; `plate_positions` by HULL_SEGMENT node id ascending; `room_surface` by tile id; `sections_of` by `section_id`; `detach_preview` by `section_id`. `wall_face_rows` returns at most 16 rows (the Failure & Trail bound `WALL_ROWS_MAX`). Cold reads that depend only on a template (`room_adjacency`, `south_band`, `plate_positions`) are precomputed once per template in the catalog row, so a read is a copy, not a recomputation.

**CONSOLE anchors (TR-derelict-034, re-tagged 2026-10-29).** `subject_anchors(section_id)` returns `SubjectAnchor` rows with `kind_hint` in `{DOOR_FACE, HARDPOINT, SOCKET, SLOT, CONSOLE, INSTRUMENT}`; `console_role` is `POD` or `DOCK` and is **present iff `kind_hint` is `CONSOLE`**. The structural lint `CONSOLE_ROLE_UNSET` (ERROR, boot-tier invariant) rejects a CONSOLE anchor without a role and a role on any other kind. The counts "each dock room holds exactly one dock status glow on its docked-podcraft prop" and "the world holds exactly four CONSOLE anchors" are **Derelict Authoring content lints** (`POD_CONSOLE_MISSING`, `DOCK_CONSOLE_MISSING`, the world-level count) evaluated over this read; Layout asserts no placement and counts nothing at runtime.

**Frame rule (TR-section-039, LY-3 c).** Every geometry read answers section-local base px; the caller composes `section_offset`. Reads that answer for one body answer in the body frame. A read never mixes frames.

### 12. Capacity, size and world-build budgets

- **Ceilings** are the registered constants and GDD knobs named in § 9, loaded from the `LayoutTuning` `ScalarTable` in the default-config data (ADR-0007 § 1.5); the module source contains no literal for any of them, and a start-up test runs the module at each knob's published minimum and maximum. Published ranges are guidance: an out-of-range value appears in the ADVISORY range report and is never clamped or asserted at boot; only schema bounds (`CONTENT_FIELD_RANGE`) and named structural invariants (`CONTENT_INVARIANT`: `area_max > 0`, `GRID_24`, `RECT_STRIDE_OVERFLOW`, `RECT_FLAGS_ILLEGAL`, `CONSOLE_ROLE_UNSET`, rotation 0) refuse a load (TR-section-033 Layout side).
- **Block size.** `bytes ~ 4 * (14 I + 10 K + 4 S + 3 B + 3)` over instance, weld, socket and body rows (D.21 with the 14th column), plus strings; `LAYOUT_BLOCK_SOFT_BYTES` raises the one-shot diagnostic `layout_block_soft_bytes`; `MAX_BLOCK_BYTES` is Save/Load's hard ceiling. The long-campaign shape (24 live and 200 tombstoned sections) is tens of KB.
- **World ceilings (TR-webmap-036 Layout half).** Layout supplies `V(room)` and the rect and door counts; the tile ceiling `TILES_WORLD_MVP`, the S0 to S4 loaded-set tile counts and `INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET` are lints and tests owned by Derelict Authoring and Web Map. A test builds the S4 loaded set through `build_section` (not a hand sum) and asserts the real `V` totals and rect counts against them. `BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME` (GDD Tuning Knobs) is the PROJECTOR's chunk size (ADR-0034); Layout's contribution is the per-section tile count.

### 13. Scene boundary and the PROJECTOR's inputs

The Layout data module references no `Node`, `Node2D`, `TileMapLayer`, `SceneTree`, `Resource` subclass or engine physics type (AC-120); a headless run leaves the orphan-node count unchanged. The PROJECTOR (`src/presentation/projector/`, ADR-0034) is a separate subscriber that never writes a block and never creates `Light2D` or `LightOccluder2D`, builds door, prop, machinery and bead/plate/scar sprites from the rect table and `welds[]`/socket state, and redraws on `SEC`, `BODY`, `SEAM` and `LEAF` keys. This ADR guarantees the three inputs of the sprite `entity_id` are stable: `section_id` (never reused, below 2^20), a closed `kind_ordinal` vocabulary (door leaf, prop, machinery, bead, plate, scar), and `template_local_idx` (the rect `idx` or the template placement index, below the rect stride and so below 2^16). The packing function and the namespace byte `LAYOUT_ID_NS` belong to ADR-0034 and the Pipeline (OQ-33); Layout exports no packing helper and tiles carry no `entity_id`.

### Key Interfaces

```gdscript

class_name LayoutIds extends RefCounted

# src/sim/layout/socket_ref.gd

(Each `class_name` is its own file. Signatures are the contract; bodies are the Layout epic's.)

### Implementation Guidelines

- **Must** register exactly one block (`layout.state`), one hook (`layout.doors`), one fault domain (4), one key space `{SEC 1, BODY 2, SEAM 3, LEAF 4}` and one diagnostics channel, only through `ModuleFacet.registrar` in `BOOTING`; **must never** register a second Layout block or a `layout.templates` block.
- **Must** store instances by reference (`template_id` plus drift hashes plus runtime fields); **must never** put geometry, a rect, a leaf, a tile list, a `kind`, a `visited` bit, a loose-item row, a door `area` or `door_state`, a float, a `layout_hash` or `mutation_count` in `layout.state`.
- **Must** snapshot as the § 2 closed key set of parallel columns, ascending ids, duplicated packed arrays; **must never** use an int-keyed `Dictionary`, `PackedStringArray`, `Vector2i`, `Rect2i`, `StringName` or `Resource` in the payload, and **must never** put a key in the payload that is not on the regenerated allow-list.
- **Must** keep `section_id == row + 1` and `body_id == row + 1`: an id is consumed only by the call that appends its row; **must never** reuse, renumber, skip or reserve an id, and **must never** let a counter wrap (the `can_*` check fails first).
- **Must** pass the Graph the section id and store the returned `{node_base, edge_base, comp_base}`; **must never** allocate a node, edge, compartment or seam id in Layout, and **must never** read the Graph's `next_*` counters except in the post-restore verification.
- **Must** compare stored hashes as `value & 0xFFFFFFFF` (`IntMath.low32`); **must never** compare a `PackedInt32Array`-read hash unmasked.
- **Must** compute the three template hashes once at catalog freeze with `Hash64.of_value` over the § 4 sub-payloads; **must never** write owner byte encoders for them (ADR-0005 `owner_canonical_byte_writer`) and **must never** store them in a template file.
- **Must** write a socket's state only inside LM2 and LM3 and choose the weld survivor by lower `body_id`; **must never** add a `set_socket_state` or `install_cap_plate` mutator, and **must never** let the result of a weld depend on argument order.
- **Must** begin every mutator with `scope.open_for(&"layout.state")`, check every Class A status, mark keys explicitly (`DirtyKey.make`) after the writes; **must never** rely on a packed-array property setter for dirty tracking (4.7), and **must never** call a Graph mutator from a `can_*` check.
- **Must** make LM2 seed each new LEAF closed with its last-projected cache and **must never** read the Graph's `area` inside LM2; **must** make `layout.doors` bump a section's `leaf_version` at most once per tick and **never** `static_version`.
- **Must** treat every door `area` write as a P2 write by command; **must never** call `set_opening_area` from a hook, and **must never** store, mirror or write `area` or `door_state` in Layout.
- **Must** use `IntMath.floor_div` for every px-to-cell, px-to-tile and leaf computation and avoid `/`, `%`, `/=`, `%=` in `src/sim/layout/`; **must never** use `float`, `Vector2`, `Rect2` or any engine geometry type in the module.
- **Must** take foot boxes as caller arguments; **must never** read `body.state` from Layout (acyclic restore, `restore_after: []`).
- **Must** make `restore` validate into scratch and copy into the existing `LayoutState`; **must never** replace the object a facade wraps, alias `data`, or return a partial restore; **must** reject `rot_q != 0` and any `structure_hash` mismatch.
- **Must** tag the hot reads of § 11 `## @hot`; **must never** allocate in `room_at`, `section_at`, `body_of`, `door_passage_into`, `leaf_would_overlap` or the hook (ADR-0010 `HOT-01`, flat `Performance.OBJECT_COUNT` over N ticks).
- **Must** keep `src/sim/layout/` scene-tree free and `src/data/` free of `src/sim/` imports; the PROJECTOR script **must never** live under `src/sim/layout/`.
- **Must** enforce capacity ceilings in `can_build`/`can_detach` before any id is consumed or the Graph is called.
- **Must** load every Layout knob from `LayoutTuning`; **must never** put a literal for a knob in module source.

content.content:
### 7. Weld offsets, bodies and the detach re-base

**Bodies.** `bodies[]` is Layout's: `{body_id, origin_section_id, state}`. **Every built section starts on its own new body at offset (0, 0), and every multi-section body is produced by welds only** (LY-25): there is no "place on an existing body" path, so the forest property holds by construction. A body's frame origin is the origin of its `origin_section_id`.

**Weld offset (D.6, TR-section-021).** `offset_b = offset_a + pos_a - pos_b`, where `a` is the **survivor-side** socket and `b` the absorbed-side socket, assigned **by body, never by argument order**: the body with the **lower `body_id`** survives (the older body; the home ship in the MVP). `attach_section` re-labels the two arguments internally, so `attach_section(x, y, ...)` and `attach_section(y, x, ...)` produce the same survivor, the same `offset_b`, the same `frame_shift_px`, and a **byte-identical** `layout.state`: the `welds[]` row always records the survivor-side section and socket as `section_a`/`socket_a` (canonicalisation). `weld_math.gd` is a pure module of integer helpers (`survivor_of`, `offset_b`, `frame_shift`) with no state, which `weld_offset(...)` (the pure read), `can_attach` and LM2 all call, so prediction and apply cannot drift.

**24-grid closure.** `pos_a`, `pos_b` and `offset_a` lie on the 24-px grid (`GRID_24` is a boot invariant, § 4), and `offset_a` does by induction from (0, 0), so `offset_b` does; an off-grid `offset_b` from a validated plan is therefore a **defect**, not a reason code: `apply` raises `LAYOUT_OFFSET_OFF_GRID` (domain 4) and returns its negative.

**LM2 effects, in order** (all inside the caller's single P2 apply, after the Graph's `weld_join`): append the `welds[]` row (`ACTIVE`); upsert both socket rows to `WELDED(seam_id)` keeping ascending order; shift every section of the absorbed body by `frame_shift_px = offset_b - offset_b_old` and move it to the survivor `body_id`; mark the absorbed body `DISSOLVED`; switch the PLATE/JAMB/LEAF slots of both sockets (§ 6); seed each newly active LEAF **closed** with its last-projected cache (§ 8); rebuild the affected broadphase handles (ADR-0014); bump `static_version` and `version` of **every section whose socket state changed (including the host section that does not move) and every moved section**; stamp `changed_region` (REGION for the two socket-host sections, FRAME for the other moved sections); cache the mated hatch's opening ids from `seam_view(seam_id).opening_ids[]` into `opening_leaves`; mark `S/<seam_id>`, `BODY/<survivor>`, `BODY/<absorbed>` and `SEC/<id>` for each affected section (5 keys for the MVP weld of two single-section bodies). The returned `AttachResult` carries `{surviving_body_id, absorbed_body_id, moved_sections[], frame_shift_px}`; `body_of` of every moved section is the survivor in the same apply and is readable by any ordered reader in the same tick.

**LM3 and the detach re-base (D.12).** After the Graph's `cut_detach`, LM3 marks the weld row `CUT_SEALED` or `CUT_RAGGED` with `cut_at_T`; sets both sockets `CAPPED` or `CUT_OPEN` (keeping `seam_id`); then **enumerates the connected components of the `ACTIVE` weld forest minus the cut seam, in ascending `section_id`**. The component containing the body's `origin_section_id` keeps its `body_id`; the other receives a new `body_id` from `next_body_id`, its `origin_section_id` is `m`, the minimum `section_id` of that component, and its offsets are re-based by `frame_shift = offset_old(m)` (`offset_new(s) = offset_old(s) - frame_shift`). The traversal uses preallocated `PackedInt32Array` stack and visited columns in `LayoutDerived`, bounded by `MAX_SECTIONS`, so no container is built in the apply. `DetachPlanner.plan(...)` is the single implementation behind both `detach_preview(seam_id)` and LM3, so the preview and the apply cannot drift (Assembly's `MSA_SHIFT_DRIFT`). A cut that does not yield exactly two components is a defect (`LAYOUT_COMPONENT_COUNT`), unreachable by the forest argument. The `DetachResult` is `{new_body_id, moved_sections[], frame_shift_px, rects[]}` with `rects[]` the cut seam's two hatch rectangles in the pre-cut body frame, **computed before the sockets change**, exactly equal to `detach_preview(seam_id).rects`. Layout performs **no actor check** (it reads nothing from `body.state`): the CHANNEL path is vetoed by Assembly's completion validate, and Body's `rebase_on_detach` is the net behind it (LY-17, BDY-24 iii).

**Why not argument order or "the larger body".** Argument order makes the dissolved body depend on a caller's mixup (the home ship could dissolve) and makes the block bytes differ between two equal worlds, which breaks AC-172 (equal blocks by different histories hash equal). "Larger body survives" would make survival depend on a count that changes with every weld. The lower `body_id` is a persisted, immutable, total order.

## GDD Requirements Addressed

TR text is `docs/architecture/tr-registry.yaml`. Section numbers are this ADR's.

### Decided here (20)

| TR-ID | Requirement | How this ADR addresses it |
|---|---|---|
| TR-section-004 | `layout.state` stores instances by reference (bodies, 13-int rows, sparse non-FREE sockets, `welds[]`, counters); derived caches never persisted | § 1, § 2: `LayoutState` vs `LayoutDerived`; closed key set; 14 columns (13 plus `structure_hash`), the one deviation |
| TR-section-005 | Ids allocated from persisted counters in template order, never reused or renumbered; tombstones; `graph_ref_base` persisted | § 2 tombstones, § 3 allocation table and rules, dense `id == row + 1` |
| TR-section-010 | Half-open integer rects with a flags byte on the 24-px grid; floor division; translation only | § 5: record, flags, frames, `GRID_24` as a boot invariant (§ 4) |

## Performance Implications
- **CPU**: `layout.doors` <= 0.2 ms at `MAX_DOORS_LOADED` on a release export (V2). Reads on the hot tier are index arithmetic and one `bsearch` at most; none allocates. LM1 to LM4 and restore are cold P2 or boundary events with a per-body grid rebuild (V3, ADR-0014); `can_attach` uncached <= 2 ms, memoised. `layout_hash()` is never per tick.
- **Memory**: the block is tens of bytes to tens of KB; `LayoutDerived` adds per-section columns of a few int64s, the socket-ref index, a bounded leaf cache (`MAX_DOORS_LOADED` slots), a small memo ring and preallocated traversal stacks sized by `MAX_SECTIONS`. Catalog templates hold the compiled rect table once per template.
- **Load Time**: three `Hash64.of_value` passes per template at catalog freeze (four templates in MVP), once. Restore validates and rebuilds in one cold pass.
- **Network**: none in MVP; `SHARED_SUMMARY` replication is the instance table plus three hashes (VS-B, ADR-0032).

## Migration Plan
There is no Layout code yet, so nothing migrates. Story order for the epic: (1) `TemplateCompiler` and the three hashes in `SectionTemplates`, with the ledger check; (2) `LayoutState`, `snapshot`/`restore`/`default_state` and the allow-list test; (3) LM1 with the `LayoutGraphPort` stub; (4) `layout.doors` and the leaf queries; (5) LM2/LM3 with the weld property tests (ADR-0021 shares them); (6) LM4 and the read views; (7) `post_restore` and verification (with ADR-0016). **GDD sync** (listed in the result and applied by the orchestrator): TR-section-004 and AC-130 to the 14-column payload and key names; LY-6 e and LY-26 e from sets to ordered sequences and the third hash; D.10, OQ-10 and the ADR-LAY-06 notes from owner TLV to payload shape; LY-32 and the key-space table to add LEAF; LY-14, LY-16, LY-17 and LY-27 for `out` records and `preview_attach`; D.21 for 14 columns; LY-26 a for nati

## Validation Criteria
- The AC-130 allow-list test (regenerated) walks the MVP snapshot and finds exactly the § 2 keys.
- Round trip: `snapshot(restore(snapshot()))` is canonical-byte identical; equal worlds built by different histories (build, weld, cut versus restore) hash equal; `mutation_count` appears in no payload (AC-172).
- Weld symmetry: `attach_section(a, b)` and `attach_section(b, a)` produce a byte-identical block and equal `AttachResult`; the lower `body_id` always survives.
- Detach: `detach_preview(seam)` equals LM3's `moved_sections`, `frame_shift_px` and `rects`; exactly two components; the property test over generated section pairs (ADR-0021) holds.
- Dense ids: build, discard and restore keep `section_id == row + 1`; a hand-edited non-dense payload fails `LAYOUT_RESTORE_COUNTER`; the section ceiling returns `CAPACITY` before any id is consumed, and counters at `2^31 - 1` never wrap.
- Drift: a room reorder fails `LAYOUT_RESTORE_TEMPLATE_CHANGED` on a fresh instance; a wall-edge edit fails on a welded instance and succeeds with `geometry_changed_fresh` on a fresh one; a visual-only edit succeeds with `visual_changed`; `rot_q = 1` fails `LAYOUT_ROT_UNSUPPORTED`; a hash at or above 2^31 compares equal after the mask.
- Leaves: a closed leaf blocks and an open one does not in the tick its state changes (P2 write, P3 read); LM2 leaves the span solid with no `stale_leaf` and no `leaf_version` bump at the first P3; an unknown opening leaves the leaf closed with one `opening_unknown`; `area > area_max` clamps with a diagnostic; at most one bump per section per tick; `static_version` never bumps from the hook; the hook's cost line (V2).
- Dirty keys: the per-mutator fixture asserts the specific keys (LM2 5, LM3 6 in D.12's example, `LEAF` from the hook) and the ADR-0004 audit raises no `MISSED_DIRTY_MARK`.
- Static scans: no `Node`/`Resource`/float/`/` in `src/sim/layout/`; no write to `sockets` columns or counters outside the named mutators; no unmasked hash compare.
- S4 loaded-set test through real `build_section` calls: tile and rect totals within the ceilings.
- Golden vectors for the three template hashes of the four MVP templates, equal on editor and export (V4).

## Related
- ADR-0001 (tick, P2/P3), ADR-0002 (no Layout command; Web Map `init_world`), ADR-0003 (block, mutators, faults), ADR-0004 (keys, audit), ADR-0005 (encoding, hashes, `IntMath`), ADR-0006 (types in a save, two-phase restore), ADR-0007 (catalog, ledger, boot tiers), ADR-0009 (presentation contract), ADR-0010 (layout, ports, lints), and `design/gdd/ship-section-and-layout-data-model.md` (owner).
- Sibling assumptions (cross-ADR): ADR-0011 provides contiguous M1 ranges in template order, the allocation-free `opening_into`, `seam_openings_into`, `section_counts_into` and `check_instantiate`, and a facade that `extends LayoutGraphPort`; ADR-0012 leaves template-door `area` untouched in P3; ADR-0014 builds the per-body broadphase from the compiled rect accessors, owns `QueryBuffer`/`OccluderSource` signatures and exposes the three counters whose bump rules are § 7 to § 8; ADR-0015 consumes `frame_shift_px`, `moved_sections`, `rects[]` and `section_at`; ADR-0016 orders restores and runs the verifiers; ADR-0021 orders Graph, Layout, Body inside one P2 apply; ADR-0026 calls LM1 in the `INIT` scope and enumerates loaded sets; ADR-0034 packs `entity_id` and chooses the redraw path on `LEAF`.
- Asks to Foundation ADRs: see the structured result (ADR-0003 check prefix; ADR-0004 key family table; ADR-0005 § 4.6 and ADR-0006 § 1.2 on `PackedStringArray` and the third hash; ADR-0007 ledger class split; ADR-0010 `LAY-*` lint rows and the port file).

## Open Questions
- **OQ-1: per-body section cap.** `can_attach` has no `BODY_FULL` reason; a merged body could exceed `MAX_FOOTPRINT_RECTS_PER_BODY`. Recommended: keep it out of MVP (the roster is a few hundred rects) and add a world lint; reopen with a `MAX_SECTIONS_PER_BODY` knob at the Vertical Slice.
- **OQ-2: traceability file.** `requirements-traceability.md` line 1367 still lists TR-derelict-034 as `ADR-0013 + ADR-0007` while row 724 says it was re-tagged to ADR-0013 alone (2026-10-29). The summary table needs the same fix; this ADR is not allowed to edit it.
- **OQ-3: `structure_hash` approval.** The deviation from "13-int rows" needs the user's confirmation; the alternative is the GDD's two hashes with the reorder defect documented as an authoring rule. The hash is not redundant with `geometry_hash`: a reorder is already caught by `geometry_hash` on an instance with history, so the third hash exists for the never-welded `FREE` instance, where `geometry_changed_fresh` would otherwise accept a reorder and silently re-point room ids, compartments and socket indices.
- **OQ-4: continuous doors.** If a stepped slide (Option B) is introduced, the hook's key-per-tick cost (R3) and the early-out need re-measuring.
- **OQ-5: Graph change counter.** Whether ADR-0011 can publish a cheap "openings changed" counter to let the hook early-out; not required for correctness.
